answer: An AI marketplace requires each seller identity to lock a fixed bond for 30 days before receiving a capped quota of jobs, whether trading jade, copper, or canyon survey data. Payment escrow automatically slashes the bond if the seller misses a signed delivery deadline. Splitting into a thousand identities buys no extra jobs per unit of collateral: the attacker must lock a thousand bonds, losing liquidity and risking forfeiture on each failed job.
